notes: OCSF class identifier (e.g. 3002 Authentication, 4001 Network Activity, 1007 Process Activity, 1001 File System Activity). Numeric taxonomy replaces UDM source_type as the per-source partition discriminator. set()/bloom-friendly; PREWHERE-eligible like UDM source_type. NOTE: `class_uid` is a real top-level OCSF field name, so the dotted-naming rule yields the same identifier (no dot).

OCSF category (1=System, 3=IAM, 4=Network Activity). Coarser than class_uid; PREWHERE for category-wide filters. Also the closest OCSF home for UDM `category` (change/event grouping) — there is no scalar OCSF `category` string.

Enum int; sibling display string is `activity` (activity_name in some emitters). class-scoped (e.g. Auth activity_id 1=Logon, File activity_id 4=Delete). Maps to UDM event_type/action. Filter on the int (fast); resolve enum-name->id at query layer.

Sibling enum string for activity_id (display + case-insensitive search). UDM action analog. Emitters serialize it as `activity_name`; activity_id is canonical. Column name `activity` is a nano-internal sibling label (not a literal OCSF path), kept for query-layer UDM `action` parity.
Most specific taxonomy id: type_uid = class_uid*100 + activity_id (e.g. 300201 = Authentication: Logon). long_t in OCSF -> UInt64. Single most-selective PREWHERE key for event-kind.
Enum int (0=Unknown,1=Informational..6=Fatal,99=Other); sibling `severity` string. UDM severity is a LowCardinality(String); here the int is canonical/indexed, string is display.
Sibling string for severity_id. Mirrors UDM severity LowCardinality(String) + set index. `severity` is a real top-level OCSF field (no dot).

OCSF `time` is epoch MILLISECONDS (timestamp_t). Convert with fromUnixTimestamp64Milli(time). NEVER compare raw ms int to DateTime64 (coerces as seconds -> far future, NAN-1123). DateTime64(3) because OCSF time is ms-precision (UDM uses (6) for micros). NOTE: this becomes the ORDER BY / partition key column; per scoping S2.4, an ORDER-BY column cannot be MATERIALIZED in CH, so this is the one column that must be DEFAULT-derived or written, not MATERIALIZED. `time_dt` is a nano bookkeeping/ALIAS name (not a literal OCSF dotted path); the physical sort-key column is `timestamp`.

Initiator IP. Stored as String (not IPv4) to match UDM src_ip storage and handle IPv4+IPv6 uniformly; lowercase-normalized at ingest like UDM src_ip. bloom_filter + PREWHERE parity with UDM. Dotted CH column name = literal OCSF path.
Responder IP. String storage to match UDM dest_ip; lowercase-normalized. bloom_filter + PREWHERE.
port_t -> UInt16, matching UDM src_port. NUMERIC field: never lower(); compare as int.
port_t -> UInt16, matching UDM dest_port. NUMERIC.
Initiator MAC (network_endpoint.mac, mac_t). Maps to UDM src_mac (bloom). lowercase-normalized to match UDM MAC storage.
Responder MAC. Maps to UDM dest_mac (bloom). lowercase-normalized.

UDM src_host is LowCardinality(String) + bloom + text(splitByNonAlpha) index + PREWHERE + lowercase-normalized. Gets `src_endpoint.hostname.search` companion. `device.hostname` is the fallback when src_endpoint absent (Host profile) - DDL may coalesce them, but src_endpoint.hostname is the primary promoted path.

Host-context hostname (Host profile / endpoint-centric classes like Process/File where there is no src_endpoint). Secondary src_host source; DDL may COALESCE(`src_endpoint.hostname`, `device.hostname`) into the canonical host column.
UDM dest_host parity: bloom + text index + PREWHERE + lowercase-normalized. `dst_endpoint.hostname.search` companion.

CLASS-DEPENDENT principal. For Authentication 3002 and IAM classes, the SUBJECT being authenticated is top-level `user.name` (required). For System Activity classes (Process 1007 / File 1001), the acting principal is `actor.user.name`. DDL should promote BOTH and the profile resolves UDM `user` to COALESCE(`user.name`, `actor.user.name`) or pick per-class. UDM user is bloom + text index + PREWHERE + lowercase-normalized. `user.name.search` companion.

Duplicate-column entry (activity_id precedent): maps UDM dest_user to the same promoted `user.name` column. Per OCSF Authentication 3002, `user` is the TARGET/subject account being acted upon and `actor.user` the initiator — exactly UDM dest_user/src_user (src_user already maps to actor.user.name). Without this, dest_user fell through to JSONExtract(event, dest_user) — a key OCSF never carries — so searches/stats/resolve_identity on it silently matched nothing (NAN-1339 follow-up from NAN-1346 #5).

The INITIATOR/actor user. In Authentication this is the impersonating/initiating user (associated with src_endpoint); in System Activity (Process/File) this is the acting user. Maps to UDM src_user; also the fallback for UDM `user` in endpoint classes. UDM src_user is bloom + text index + lowercase-normalized. `actor.user.name.search` companion.
UDM user_domain is lowercase-normalized (skip lower() wrapper). Class-dependent sibling of user.name.
OCSF user.uid is a string_t (SID/UPN/objectGUID), not numeric -> ch String (UDM user_id is numeric in inference but OCSF uid is opaque string; store as String). bloom for pivots.

PARENT/INITIATOR process name. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007, top-level `process` is the SUBJECT (the launched/terminated process) and `actor.process` is the PARENT/initiator that acted on it. So `actor.process.name` is the parent — secondary, no UDM alias (udm_field=null). UDM process_name now resolves to the primary `process.name`. bloom + text index + PREWHERE + lowercase-normalized retained for parent-process pivots/hunts.

PRIMARY subject process name. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007, top-level `process` is the SUBJECT (launched/injected/terminated). This is the canonical UDM process_name ('what ran'); the parent is `actor.process.name`. bloom + text index + lowercase-normalized.

PARENT/INITIATOR command line. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007, `actor.process` is the PARENT/initiator, so its cmd_line IS the UDM parent_command_line. OCSF uses `cmd_line` (not command_line). text(splitByNonAlpha) index for full-text parent-cmd hunts.

PRIMARY subject command line. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007, top-level `process` is the SUBJECT, so its cmd_line IS the UDM command_line ('what ran'); the parent is `actor.process.cmd_line`. text(splitByNonAlpha) index + full-text hunt parity (e.g. 'System32').

PRIMARY subject process pid. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007 the SUBJECT is top-level `process`, so process.pid (integer_t -> UInt32) IS the UDM process_id. NUMERIC. The parent pid is `actor.process.pid`.

PARENT process pid. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007 `actor.process` is the parent/initiator; secondary, no UDM alias (udm_field=null — UDM process_id now resolves to the subject `process.pid`). OCSF process.pid (integer_t) -> UInt32. NUMERIC.

PRIMARY subject process uid — OCSF-native process identifier (process_t.uid, string_t). Per OCSF Process Activity 1007 the SUBJECT is top-level `process`, so process.uid IS the UDM process_guid analog (client-provided GUID, NOT recomputed). bloom for process-tree pivots. The parent uid is `actor.process.uid`.

PARENT process uid (process_t.uid, string_t). Per OCSF Process Activity 1007 `actor.process` is the parent/initiator, so its uid maps to UDM parent_process_guid (NAN-1346 tree lineage; mirrors parent_command_line → actor.process.cmd_line). UDM process_guid resolves to the subject `process.uid`. bloom for process-tree pivots.

PRIMARY subject process hash. ARRAY flatten: process.file.hashes is an array of fingerprint{algorithm_id,value}; pick algorithm_id=3 (SHA-256) -> .value. Per OCSF Process Activity 1007 the SUBJECT is top-level `process`, so this IS the UDM process_hash (bloom). MATERIALIZED expr uses arrayFirst over the JSON array to select SHA-256, lowercased to match UDM hash dict-key convention. The parent hash is `actor.process.file.hashes.sha256`. No scalar OCSF path -> array-derived convention `<path>.sha256`.
Subject process image path (Process Activity 1007). UDM process_path.
Initiator/parent process image path; also the acting-process image on module/network/file/dns/registry classes. UDM parent_process_path.

PARENT process hash. ARRAY flatten: actor.process.file.hashes fingerprint[] -> algorithm_id=3 (SHA-256). Per OCSF Process Activity 1007 `actor.process` is the parent/initiator; secondary, no UDM alias (udm_field=null — UDM process_hash now resolves to the subject `process.file.hashes.sha256`). Still bloom + lowercased (parent-hash pivots / prevalence summary). Array-derived convention `<path>.sha256`.
File System Activity 1001 `file` is the target. UDM file_name has bloom index.
UDM file_path has text(splitByNonAlpha) index + `.search` companion (path-fragment hunts). file.path ~= UDM file_path.

ARRAY flatten: file.hashes is fingerprint[]; pick algorithm_id=3 (SHA-256). There is NO scalar file_hash in OCSF. Maps to UDM file_hash (bloom). MATERIALIZED arrayFirst over JSON array; lowercase to match UDM hash convention. Multi-algo (MD5=1, SHA1=2, SHA512=4) stay in the event tail. Column name = array-derived convention `<path>.sha256`.
Loaded module image path (Module Activity 1005). OCSF-native; no UDM equivalent.
Loaded module file name (Module Activity 1005).

On File System Activity 1001, the file action (Create=1, Read=2, Update=3, Delete=4, Rename=5, Open=14...) is encoded in activity_id (same column as the taxonomy activity_id above). UDM file_action is class-scoped to the activity enum; no separate column - reuses activity_id with class_uid=1001 context.

IANA protocol number (integer_t, -1 default for unknown -> Int32). UDM protocol is a lowercase-normalized string; here the int is canonical. The sibling string OCSF path is `connection_info.protocol_ver`/`network_protocol`; promote protocol_num as the indexed value, surface UDM `protocol` string via profile mapping.
long_t -> UInt64, matching UDM bytes_in. NUMERIC.
long_t -> UInt64, matching UDM bytes_out. NUMERIC.
long_t -> UInt64, matching UDM packets_in. NUMERIC.
long_t -> UInt64, matching UDM packets_out. NUMERIC.
Authentication 3002 only. Enum int (1=NTLM,2=Kerberos,5=SAML,6=OAUTH 2.0,...,99=Other); sibling string `auth_protocol`. Maps to UDM auth_type. Filter on int (fast); string for display.
Sibling enum string for auth_protocol_id. Display + case-insensitive search; auth_protocol_id is canonical for filtering. `auth_protocol` is a real top-level OCSF field (no dot).
Generic outcome enum (1=Success, 2=Failure, 0=Unknown, 99=Other) present on base_event, used across classes. Maps to UDM auth_result / status. Sibling string `status`. Filter on int.

Sibling enum string for status_id (Success/Failure/...). Maps to UDM status. UDM status is set-indexed; mirror with set index. status_id is canonical for filtering. `status` is a real top-level OCSF field (no dot).
session object uid. Maps to UDM session_id (String).

Human-readable summary. UDM message has text(splitByNonAlpha) index + `message.search` companion (the primary full-text hunt field). `raw_data` (unparsed) stays in the event tail / maps to a secondary column if needed. `message` is a real top-level OCSF field (no dot).

OCSF url object has `hostname` (the domain) + `path` + full `url_string`. Top-level `url` is carried by Network Activity 4001 (and other classes with a url object), NOT by HTTP Activity 4002. So this is the network-activity URL domain — secondary, no UDM alias (udm_field=null); UDM url_domain now resolves to the HTTP `http_request.url.hostname`. bloom-indexed domain entity for IOC/prevalence pivots on 4001.

Full URL string for Network Activity 4001 (top-level `url` object). OCSF 1.8.0 url object's full-URL attribute is `url_string`. Secondary, no UDM alias (udm_field=null); UDM url now resolves to the HTTP `http_request.url.url_string`. text index for URL-fragment hunts on 4001.
HTTP Activity 4002. http_request.http_method (GET/POST/...). Maps to UDM http_method (set(20) index). LowCardinality.

HTTP Activity 4002 URL domain. HTTP Activity 4002 has NO top-level `url`; the URL lives at `http_request.url.*`. So the UDM url_domain for HTTP is `http_request.url.hostname` (the prior top-level `url.hostname` is empty for HTTP and now serves only Network Activity 4001). bloom-indexed domain entity for IOC/prevalence pivots. NOT lower()'d (matches the top-level url.hostname convention).

HTTP Activity 4002 full URL string. HTTP Activity 4002 has NO top-level `url`; the URL lives at `http_request.url.*`. So the UDM url for HTTP is `http_request.url.url_string` (mirrors the top-level url.url_string, which now serves only Network Activity 4001). text index for URL-fragment hunts.

HTTP Activity 4002. The requested URL path component (url object's `path`). Secondary, no UDM alias (udm_field=null); UDM url for HTTP now resolves to the full `http_request.url.url_string`. text index for path-fragment hunts. (UDM url_domain on HTTP lives at http_request.url.hostname.)
HTTP Activity 4002. http_request.user_agent. Maps to UDM http_user_agent (text(splitByNonAlpha) index + `.search` companion for UA-substring hunts).
HTTP Activity 4002. http_response.code (integer_t HTTP status, e.g. 200/404/500) -> UInt16, matching UDM http_status_code. NUMERIC.

DNS Activity 4003. query.hostname is the queried domain (dns_query.hostname, required). Maps to UDM `query` (text(splitByNonAlpha) index + `.search` companion for domain-fragment hunts). Also a domain entity for IOC/prevalence pivots.

DNS Activity 4003. answers is a dns_answer[] array; rdata holds the resolved record data (IP for A/AAAA, target for CNAME). There is no scalar OCSF answer - we promote the FIRST answer's rdata to match UDM `answer` (bloom). array_key with null key_attr/key_value signals 'take the first element's value_attr' (no algorithm-id selector). Multi-answer tail stays in event. Column name = array-derived `<path>.rdata`.
Email Activity 4009. email.from (email_t single value). Maps to UDM sender (bloom). lowercase-normalized (email addresses).

Email Activity 4009. email.to is an email_address ARRAY. UDM recipient is a scalar; we promote the FIRST recipient to match UDM (bloom), additional recipients stay in the event tail. array_key with null key_attr AND null value_attr signals 'take the first element directly' (the array holds scalar strings, not objects). lowercase-normalized.
Email Activity 4009. email.subject. Maps to UDM subject (text(splitByNonAlpha) index + `.search` companion for subject-keyword hunts).

Email Activity 4009. email.message_uid is the RFC5322 Message-ID. Maps to UDM message_id (bloom). NOTE: OCSF email.uid is the email THREAD id (different concept) - left in the tail; message_uid is the per-message id matching UDM message_id.

FINDING-CLASS ONLY (Vulnerability Finding 2002 and other Finding classes carry vulnerabilities[]). vulnerabilities is an array of vulnerability objects; vulnerability.cve.uid is the CVE id (e.g. CVE-2021-12345). UDM cve is scalar; we promote the FIRST vuln's cve.uid (bloom). array_key value_attr is a DOTTED sub-path 'cve.uid' resolved within the first array element; null key_attr/key_value = take first element. Multi-CVE tail stays in event. Non-finding events leave this empty. Column name = array-derived `<path>.cve.uid`.

OCSF `cloud` object (Cloud profile, attaches to many classes). cloud.provider (required). Maps to UDM cloud_provider (set(20) index). LowCardinality. CLIENT-POPULATED (read) or nano-populated (compute) - cloud is part of the standard OCSF record either way (dual-mode enrichment note in DDL header).
cloud.account is an Account object; account.uid is the cloud account/subscription id. Maps to UDM cloud_account_id (bloom).
cloud.account.name. Maps to UDM cloud_account_name (set(500) index). LowCardinality.
cloud.region (recommended). Maps to UDM cloud_region (set(100) index). LowCardinality.

API Activity 6003 (and other classes carrying the `api` object). `api.service` is a Service object (verified against OCSF 1.8.0 objects/api -> objects/service: service.name is string_t, recommended); service.name is the cloud/AWS service the call targeted (e.g. 'signin', 'sts', 's3', 'ec2'). Maps to UDM cloud_service. Low-cardinality service axis -> LowCardinality + set(100) index. CLIENT-POPULATED. Distinct from cloud.provider (the CSP) and api.operation (the verb).

API Activity 6003 (and other classes carrying the `api` object). `api.operation` (verified against OCSF 1.8.0 objects/api: operation is string_t, recommended) is the API verb the call invoked — for AWS CloudTrail this is the eventName (e.g. 'CreateAccessKey', 'AssumeRole', 'AttachUserPolicy', 'PutBucketPolicy'). NO UDM equivalent: there is no scalar UDM field for the cloud action verb, so this is a native OCSF-only promotion (udm_field=null). The cloud action allow-lists reference the native `api.operation` column directly under the OCSF profile (the generic `activity` Create/Read/Update/Delete enum is too coarse for these AWS-verb filters). Low-cardinality verb axis -> LowCardinality + set(100) index. CLIENT-POPULATED. Distinct from api.service.name (the targeted service) and the activity_id taxonomy (the CRUD class).

API Activity 6003. `resources` is a resource_details[] array (verified against OCSF 1.8.0 classes/api_activity -> objects/resource_details). UDM resource_type is scalar; we promote the FIRST resource's `type` (resource_details.type, string_t, optional — the source-defined resource type, e.g. 'AWS::S3::Bucket', 'AWS::IAM::Role'). array_key with null key_attr/key_value = take first element; value_attr 'type' selects the sub-field. Multi-resource tail stays in event. Low-cardinality -> LowCardinality + set(200). Column name = array-derived convention `<path>.type`.

API Activity 6003. resources[] resource_details[]; we promote the FIRST resource's `uid` (resource_details.uid, recommended — the unique resource identifier, e.g. an ARN / resource OCID). UDM resource_id (bloom for resource pivots). array_key null key_attr/key_value = first element; value_attr 'uid'. Column name = array-derived `<path>.uid`.

API Activity 6003. resources[] resource_details[]; we promote the FIRST resource's `name` (resource_details.name, recommended — the human resource name). UDM resource_name (bloom). array_key null key_attr/key_value = first element; value_attr 'name'. Column name = array-derived `<path>.name`.

VALUE-SEMANTICS CAVEAT (like auth_result string->int). On API Activity 6003 the change action is encoded in activity_id (Create=1, Read=2, Update=3, Delete=4, Unknown=0, Other=99) — there is NO scalar OCSF `change_type` string column. UDM change_type values are 'permission_change' | 'create' | 'delete' | 'update'. Partial mapping ONLY: create<->1, update<->3, delete<->4. UDM 'permission_change' has NO OCSF activity_id equivalent (it is a UDM-specific normalization, not in the 6003 enum), and OCSF activity_id=2 (Read) has no UDM change_type. So change_type is class-scoped to activity_id with class_uid=6003 (reuses the shared activity_id column, exactly like file_action reuses it for class_uid=1001) and the query layer must translate enum int<->UDM string with the lossy mapping above; 'permission_change' is unrepresentable and must be derived from richer context (api.operation / resource type) at the query layer, NOT from this column. NO new column is added — this is a documented reuse of the existing taxonomy activity_id.

Authentication 3002 only. OCSF `is_mfa` is a boolean_t (verified against OCSF 1.8.0 classes/authentication: is_mfa, boolean, recommended) indicating whether MFA was used. Promoted as UInt8 (0/1) to match UDM mfa_used boolean storage. NUMERIC — never lower()'d. JSONExtractBool/JSONExtractUInt over event.is_mfa. No skip index (low-selectivity 2-value boolean; mirrors UDM mfa_used which carries no dedicated skip index).

DUAL-MODE ENRICHMENT. OCSF location.country is the ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 code (verified: 'US','CA'), so it maps to UDM enriched_src_country_code (NOT the country NAME column). Geo lives in the OCSF-native location object whether nano computed it (open-core ingestion) or the client shipped it pre-enriched. set(200) index parity with UDM enriched_src_country_code. NOTE: UDM also has a country-NAME column (enriched_src_country); OCSF location has no separate name attribute, so the name column is left in the event tail / derived at query layer (see README deferred note).

DUAL-MODE. location.continent is the continent NAME. Maps to UDM enriched_src_continent (set(10) index). OCSF location has no continent_code attribute -> UDM enriched_src_continent_code is deferred to the tail.

DUAL-MODE. autonomous_system.number (Integer ASN). UDM enriched_src_asn is a String; here the OCSF-native ASN is numeric -> UInt32 (bloom). The SQL generator surfaces it as the UDM asn concept. NUMERIC.
DUAL-MODE. autonomous_system.name (org name). Maps to UDM enriched_src_as_name (bloom). OCSF AS object has no as_domain attribute -> UDM enriched_src_as_domain deferred to tail.
DUAL-MODE. dst_endpoint geo ISO country code -> UDM enriched_dest_country_code. set(200).
DUAL-MODE. dst continent name -> UDM enriched_dest_continent. set(10).
DUAL-MODE. dst ASN number -> UDM enriched_dest_asn (bloom). NUMERIC.
DUAL-MODE. dst AS org name -> UDM enriched_dest_as_name (bloom).

DUAL-MODE IOC. OCSF-native enrichments[] is an array of {name,value,type,provider,data}. We select by NAME: arrayFirst(e -> name='ioc_src_ip_threat_type', enrichments).value. The enrichment NAME is the UDM column name (the contract: nano writes enrichments[] entries named after the UDM ioc_*/custom_* column; clients shipping pre-enriched OCSF use the same names). array_key uses key_value_str (a STRING key) instead of key_value (int) - the DDL emits a string arrayFirst and the consistency test handles either shape. Maps to UDM ioc_src_ip_threat_type (bloom).
DUAL-MODE IOC. enrichments[name='ioc_dest_ip_threat_type'].value -> UDM ioc_dest_ip_threat_type (bloom).
DUAL-MODE IOC. enrichments[name='ioc_domain_threat_type'].value -> UDM ioc_domain_threat_type (bloom).
DUAL-MODE IOC. enrichments[name='ioc_hash_threat_type'].value -> UDM ioc_hash_threat_type (bloom).

DUAL-MODE CUSTOM. enrichments[name='custom_src_ip_tags'].value -> UDM custom_src_ip_tags. UDM stores this as Array(String); the enrichments[] value is a String (comma/JSON-joined tags) so we promote it as String + bloom (the UDM Array semantics are reconstructed at the query layer). Covers the UDM-indexed custom_* enrichment_value_* footprint via the generic by-name selector.
DUAL-MODE CUSTOM. enrichments[name='custom_dest_ip_tags'].value -> UDM custom_dest_ip_tags (bloom).

THE OCSF SOURCE IDENTIFIER (source_type analog). metadata.product.name (object_type=product, scalar string_t; verified against OCSF 1.8.0 objects/product + objects/metadata at schema.ocsf.io) is the reporting product that emitted the event — e.g. 'apache http server', 'Conduit Proxy', 'Microsoft Sysmon'. Maps to UDM vendor_product (the product field). bloom_filter + PREWHERE=true: this is the per-source axis the UI's source/source_type selector should read for OCSF rows, DISTINCT from class_uid (which is the event CLASS, not the origin product). Case is preserved (NOT lower()'d) — product name is a display label, unlike host/user/ip. Dotted CH column name = literal OCSF path.

metadata.product.vendor_name (string_t) — the vendor of the reporting product (e.g. 'Apache', 'nano', 'Microsoft'). Low-cardinality vendor axis; set index. No direct UDM column (UDM folds vendor+product into vendor_product); kept as provenance for source-grouping. Case preserved.

metadata.product.feature.name (feature object_t under product; feature.name is string_t; verified against OCSF 1.8.0 objects/feature) — the product feature / log-type sub-source (e.g. 'access_log', 'WAF', 'mod_security'). Finer-grained than product.name. No UDM analog -> udm_field null; pure provenance. bloom_filter for sub-source pivots. Case preserved.
metadata.log_name (string_t) — the log channel / file name the event was read from (e.g. 'Security', '/var/log/apache2/access.log'). No UDM analog -> udm_field null; provenance. bloom_filter.

metadata.log_provider (string_t) — the logging provider / collector that produced the log (e.g. 'Vector', 'Syslog', 'Windows Event Log'). Low-cardinality -> LowCardinality + set index. No UDM analog -> udm_field null; provenance.

metadata.uid (string_t) — the unique event identifier assigned by the producer. Provenance / lookup / dedup key; the OCSF analog of UDM id/event_id (opaque String, not a CH UUID). bloom_filter for by-id lookup pivots. Case preserved.

metadata.version (string_t) — the OCSF schema version of the record (e.g. '1.8.0'). REQUIRED in OCSF. Provenance only; no UDM analog -> udm_field null. Extremely low cardinality -> LowCardinality + set index.

metadata.correlation_uid (string_t) — the producer-assigned correlation id grouping related events. Provenance / pivot key; no UDM analog -> udm_field null. bloom_filter for correlation pivots. Case preserved.

Ingest-time host_count for the file SHA-256 against the SCHEMA-AGNOSTIC nanosiem.hash_prevalence_dict (NAN-1248). Real promoted column (UInt16) mirroring UDM logs.prevalence_file_hash byte-for-byte: 1-9998 = actual host count, 9999 = common/not-tracked, 65535 = no hash present. Keyed on file.hashes.sha256 (already lowercased at ingest). Powers asset-card prevalence parity. NUMERIC — never lower()'d.

Ingest-time host_count for the subject process SHA-256 against nanosiem.hash_prevalence_dict (NAN-1248). Mirrors UDM logs.prevalence_process_hash. Keyed on process.file.hashes.sha256 (the SUBJECT process hash, lowercased at ingest) — per OCSF Process Activity 1007 `process` is the subject and `actor.process` is the parent. NUMERIC.

Ingest-time host_count for the destination hostname against nanosiem.domain_prevalence_dict (NAN-1248). Mirrors UDM logs.prevalence_dest_domain. Keyed on lower(dst_endpoint.hostname); skipped (65535) for IPv4-literal dest hostnames. NUMERIC.

Ingest-time host_count for the destination IP against nanosiem.ip_prevalence_dict (NAN-1248). Mirrors UDM logs.prevalence_dest_ip. Keyed on dst_endpoint.ip; skipped (65535) for RFC1918/loopback ranges. NUMERIC.
